description: Live talk dashboard: the same memory seen by process, cgroup, kubelet and host kernel. Each number answers a different question.

options.content: # Same node, same moment: who's right?

panels.description: Which 'memory used' is right? The host counts page cache as available; the kubelet counts it as used.
panels.title: Host used vs Kubernetes node usage

panels.description: Positive: page cache dominates. Negative: kernel/driver memory dominates. Near zero: coincidence, not agreement.
panels.title: Δ = k8s usage − host used
2 · Working set: what the kubelet acts on

options.content: # working set = usage − inactive file pages

panels.description: How much of the node's memory is in use, from most to least inclusive? usage includes all cache; working_set drops inactive file pages; rss is anonymous memory only.
panels.title: Node: usage vs working set vs rss vs host used

panels.description: What does the kubelet subtract? Only the grey band; everything below it counts toward eviction.
panels.title: What's inside node usage

panels.description: Which 'available' triggers eviction? The kubelet evicts based on the teal line, not the purple one.
panels.title: How close is eviction?

panels.description: Is the kubelet's node 'limit' the host's MemTotal? Yes, even inside kind, where the node is just a container.
panels.title: Kubelet's MemTotal vs host MemTotal

panels.description: Is 'node' everything on the machine? 'pods' is only part of it; kubelet, runtime and misc are the rest.
panels.title: Node breakdown by system container
3 · Pods & containers: same formula, different input

options.content: # The collector's container usage = memory.current. Every charged page, active or inactive.

panels.description: Where does OOM risk live? Between the green and the blue line. The kernel kills on memory.current vs limit after reclaim, not on working set.
panels.title: Container: usage vs working set vs rss vs limit

panels.description: What do dashboards usually alert on? Working set / limit. A high value can still be mostly reclaimable active cache.
panels.title: Working set vs limit

options.content: # RSS ≠ RSS. The collector's process RSS includes its binary; Kubernetes rss doesn't.

panels.description: Does k8s rss match the process? k8s rss ≈ process RssAnon. The binary's pages (RssFile) aren't in k8s rss, but they are in working_set, because mapped code pages are active.
panels.title: Collector: process view vs container view

panels.description: What does the process have in RAM? anon + file + shmem; shared pages are counted again in every process.
panels.title: Process VmRSS

panels.description: How much of the process is its own binary? Mapped file pages, reclaimable when clean.
panels.title: Process RssFile

panels.description: What does Kubernetes call rss? Only anonymous memory, about the process RssAnon.
panels.title: k8s container rss

panels.description: What does Kubernetes act on? Includes the binary's active mapped pages.
panels.title: k8s container working_set

panels.description: Why is process RSS so much bigger than Kubernetes rss? For static Go binaries most RSS is file-backed: the executable's own code and read-only data. Reclaimable when clean.
panels.title: Process RSS by type

panels.description: How much can't be dropped for free? Dirty pages need writeback or swap before reclaim, roughly the process's OOM-relevant floor.
panels.title: Dirty memory (can't be dropped for free)

options.content:
## rss → Is the collector growing? (leaks, trends)
## working_set → Will Kubernetes act on the collector? (eviction, limit headroom)
## usage → Don't alert on it

panels.description: Is my app growing? A steadily positive slope means allocation without release. Ignore the absolute value, watch the trend.
panels.title: rss trend (leak detector)

panels.description: How close is each container to its limit, as Kubernetes sees it? Working set / limit with the 90% line.
panels.title: Headroom: working set vs limit

panels.description: What should you page on, warn on, diagnose with?

options.content:
- **Page on outcomes:** OOMKilled, evictions, node MemoryPressure
- **Warn on leading indicators:** working_set/limit > 90%, node available near the eviction threshold, PSI
- **Diagnose with:** rss vs working_set (cache vs real growth); host MemAvailable vs kubelet available (invisible kernel memory)
- **Never alert on usage**

panels.title: Alerting layers

panels.description: How do the other Go binaries compare? Same anon / file / shmem split for kubelet, containerd, etcd, kube-apiserver and the collector.
panels.title: Process RSS by type: other Go binaries

title: Linux & Kubernetes Memory: Who Measures It?
